audience.text: Java developers building or inspecting 3D scenes who need a free, open-source library with API compatibility to Aspose.3D for Java, targeting Java 21 or later.

capabilities.text: Developers construct scenes using Scene, organize nodes via createChildNode and addChildNode, and attach geometry using addEntity.
capabilities.title: Build and traverse 3D scene graphs

capabilities.text: The library supports binary and ASCII STL import and export through Scene.fromFile and Scene.save with StlLoadOptions and StlSaveOptions.
capabilities.title: Import and export STL geometry

capabilities.text: Developers create PbrMaterial instances with albedo, metallic, roughness, emissive, and occlusion properties, and assign them via Node.setMaterial.
capabilities.title: Define materials and assign them to nodes

capabilities.text: NurbsCurve exposes control points, knot vectors, degree, and curve type; control points are added using Vector4.
capabilities.title: Model NURBS curves with control points

capabilities.text: The library provides Vector2, Vector3, Vector4, Matrix4, Quaternion, and BoundingBox for geometry and transform math.
capabilities.title: Perform 3D math operations

capabilities.text: FileFormat.detect enables automatic format detection from file paths or streams, and FileFormat.getFormatByExtension resolves format from extension.
capabilities.title: Detect file format automatically

limitations.text: STL is the only format with fully functional import and export in the published 26.5.0 package; other formats have stub implementations.
OBJ import is not functional in the published package despite having a parser in the upstream source; developers must build from source to use it.
NURBS curve sampling is not implemented; only control point and knot vector data are exposed.
Scene rendering is not implemented in this edition.

problems_solved.text: Provides a free, open-source alternative to the commercial Aspose.3D for Java library for basic 3D scene graph operations and STL format I/O.
Enables automatic format detection and explicit format resolution for 3D files via FileFormat.detect and FileFormat.getFormatByExtension.
Supports building 3D scenes using primitives like Box, Cylinder, Sphere, and Dish, each implementing toMesh() to produce Mesh geometry.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Java is a clean-room, MIT-licensed Java library implementing a 3D scene graph API compatible with the commercial Aspose.3D for Java product, exposing the com.aspose.threed.* package.

uncertainties: The README mentions OBJ import is not functional in the published package but does not clarify whether the upstream source includes a working parser.
It is unclear whether FileFormat.WAVEFRONTOBJ is fully implemented in the published artifact or only in the upstream source.
The exact set of formats with stub implementations beyond OBJ and STL is not fully specified in the facts.
It is unclear whether PbrSpecularMaterial accessors are present but unimplemented or entirely absent in the published package.
The behavior of loading or saving through unrecognized formats is described as failing silently, but no specific examples are provided in the facts.
The relationship between the FOSS edition and the commercial edition's API surface beyond com.aspose.threed.* is not detailed in the facts.
It is unclear whether the test suite covers all public symbols listed in the API reference section of the README.
The exact scope of excluded functionality such as License, Metered, cryptographic helpers, and ZIP-packaged file-system read/write is not fully detailed in the facts.

workflows.name: Build and test from source
workflows.text: Developers build the project using mvn package and run tests with mvn test; CI workflows are defined in .github/workflows/.

workflows.name: Load and convert STL files
workflows.text: Developers load an STL file using Scene.fromFile and save it using Scene.save, optionally specifying StlLoadOptions or StlSaveOptions.

workflows.name: Define NURBS curves
workflows.text: Developers create NurbsCurve instances, set degree and control points using Vector4, and access knot vectors and curve type data.
